evidence.note: First action was to launch a 9,000-step run of a near-final-scale 29.57M-param model — no tiny end-to-end pipeline was validated first, so scaling and correctness were entangled in the initial monolithic push (the opposite of baseline-first).
Size done-check (29.72MB < 32MB cap) was verified early at step 500 within the first run — a genuine, if in-run, gate baked into the script.

Contract/load-via-grader-interface, forward/loss verification, and accurate baseline val_bpb were measured only AFTER the full 9k run completed, not before committing to scale — correctness locking came late.

Improvement phase had clear per-experiment gates: 12-layer and big-int4 runs each checked size at step 500 and were compared against the saved 9-layer baseline, with backups kept and restore-if-worse fallbacks — phased structure with rough success criteria.
Final n-gram wrapper phase treated as a discrete experiment with a bpb done-check (0.98164 < 0.983) and contract re-verification before submit, showing sustained phasing to the end.

reasoning: The agent showed clear ordered phases with real done-checks (early size gate, explicit load/contract verification, baseline bpb measurement, and improvement experiments gated by comparison to a backed-up baseline with fallbacks), which exceeds pure implicit ordering (anchor 3). However, the central baseline-first behavior of anchor 5 — getting a *small* model training end-to-end and verifying save/load/quantize/contract BEFORE committing capacity — was absent: the very first action was a full-scale 9k-step run, and contract correctness was verified only after it finished, entangling scaling with correctness. This places the trajectory at a 4, interpolating between anchors 3 and 5.
